seed: Objects of type `target` under action ACTION3 with touching neighbours [reflection] show mixed outcomes: h,pixels,w,y x1, h,pixels,w,x,y x1. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: the exact click position relative to the object, when the action is a click. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Board = 21x21 blocks of 3x3 read from frame corners: wall axis (10) at one block row, pieces (5 ring), targets (solid 11), reflections (4) of piece blocks r!=A at 2A-r, skipped on piece blocks / off board.
A1/A2 move selected axis (bounds only, passes under pieces) or selected piece (A1-A4, blocked by edge and other pieces); A3/A4 with axis selected are no-ops; A5 cycles axis -> pieces by size desc -> axis.
Render per block: ring = topmost of piece>reflection>target>wall>bg 9; centre = 11 if target present, else first fill top-down (selected piece 0, reflection 4, selected wall 0), else 9.
HUD: column 63 rows 0-62 turn 11->12 top-down, one cell per action that changed the board. Hidden state (piece split) gated on frame continuity; stateless fallback also passes 29/29.
Target A3 mixed-outcome hypothesis was a red herring (just occlusion re-render); unconfirmed: whether blocked piece moves tick the HUD, A5 order beyond the first piece, A6/A7, win/level change.
